subject: Recap: ClearBank inference economics & pilot success criteria
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@clearbank.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Recap: ClearBank inference economics & pilot success criteria

Hi Samir / Clara —

Thanks again for the conversation earlier — good to learn more about the ClearBank fraud-scoring flow and where inference spend is creating pressure. Per our call, I wanted to capture the pain points, measured goals, and next steps so we have a shared starting point for the pilot. Please flag anything I missed.

Key pain points you mentioned:
- Unit token costs are spiking during peak hours when the transaction-scoring model runs with long context (~2.5k tokens) across user/session history.
- Current infra is single-region (us-east) and you have tight latency SLOs for pre-auth scoring (<120ms 95th).
- Existing system does occasional batch re-score runs overnight but little prefix/KV caching for interactive flows.
- Ops overhead: managing model variants and quantization tradeoffs is a blocker — team prefers recommendations not tooling-heavy dev work.

Success criteria for a pilot (what would make this a win):
1) Reduce average per-1k token inference cost by >=40% vs today while keeping 95th latency under 120ms for interactive calls.
2) Demonstrate safe throughput scaling to 120 QPS for the scoring endpoint with graceful degradation during bursts.
3) Show production-quality end-to-end integration (prefix caching + fallbacks) with no change to ClearBank auth flow logic.
4) Quantized model variant that preserves AUC within 0.5% of your baseline model.

Technical assumptions we discussed:
- Typical interactive requests: 800–2,800 token windows; batchable but latency-sensitive.
- Nightly batch re-score: large seq lengths (20k tokens) processed in bulk.
- Willingness to try 4-bit/QLoRA-style quantization if we run a small eval set first.

Proposed next steps (we can kickoff the pilot once these are agreed):
- ClearBank: share a 24–48h anonymized sample of scoring traces and a short test set for AUC validation (we suggested SFTP or Google Drive link).
- Redwood: provide a cost model and pilot scope doc (attached), plus a short infra checklist for private connectivity and keys.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with your infra team (30–45m) next week to confirm KV cache placement and fallback policies.
- Declare target timelines: 2-week benchmarking + 4-week integration pilot (proposal in attachment).

Attachments: clearbank-pilot-scope.xlsx (pilot milestones & measurement plan), redwood-cost-assumptions.pdf (unit economics & quantization options).

If that aligns, I’ll open the pilot SR and loop in our performance engineer to schedule the deep dive.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
laura@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Recap: ClearBank inference economics & pilot success criteria

Laura —

This looks great and captures the high-level objectives. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Latency SLO is 120ms P95 for the pre-auth path; for non-blocking async scoring we can accept 500ms.
- The nightly batch job is ~100k messages and is not latency-sensitive; if quantizing helps cost there it's fine.
- Security: we will need SOC2 evidence + a short network diagram before we exchange test traces; Clara will coordinate.

I’ll aim to share a redacted 48h trace by Tue (link or sftp) and will work with Clara on the checklist. Appreciate the pilot doc — will review and circle back.

Best,
Samir
Director, Fraud Engineering | ClearBank
samir@clearbank.com

Date: 2026-10-11T18:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap: ClearBank inference economics & pilot success criteria

Thanks Samir — good clarifications, noted. A couple quick answers to keep momentum:

- SOC2 / security: I attached a short ops checklist; we can provide SOC2 summary and a redacted architecture diagram once Clara confirms scope.
- Quantization: we'll run a small A/B on your validation set (10–20k examples) to measure AUC delta; if 4-bit increases error >0.5% we’ll try mixed precision or selective quantization (embedding/attenuation).
- Cost target framing: our preliminary model (attached) shows a plausible 35–50% unit cost reduction via prefix caching + 4-bit quantization + workload-aware batching depending on token distribution. We’ll refine once we see the traces.

Proposed deep-dive times (PST): Mon 10/14 10:00am or Tue 10/15 2:00pm — can you & infra team confirm availability?

If agreed I’ll send a calendar invite and drop the onboarding checklist in a shared Drive.

Regards,
Laura
